title: Security spec-text corrections in 06-security: RFC 6979 nonce mislabel, EDHOC exporter label phrasing, fresh-PIV interop-vector claim (R-06-004/209/221)
description: Three spec-text accuracy items in spec/06-security.md found this sweep (spec fixes, not code): (1) §8.3 line 61 'Deterministic nonce (RFC 6979) REQUIRED' — RFC 6979 is HMAC-DRBG-based; the normative pseudocode at line 65 (r = H(privkey‖msg) mod L) is the Ed25519-style hash construction and ALL three stacks implement exactly that (python schnorr48.py:132, C schnorr48.c:80-91, rust schnorr48 crate). Fix: relabel as deterministic hash-based nonce per draft-lichen-schnorr-00, drop the RFC 6979 attribution or amend the draft wording. (2) §8.9 lines 526-527 write EDHOC-Exporter('OSCORE Master Secret',...) / ('OSCORE Master Salt',...) — implementations use RFC 9528 §7.2 numeric labels 0/1 (16/8 bytes; edhoc_export_rfc9529.json oracle); rephrase spec to the numeric labels. (3) §15.3 line 1466 claims 'interop vectors pin the fresh-PIV requirement (no first-notification-omission case is valid)' — no such vector exists (test/vectors/coap_observe_sequence.json pins RFC 7641 only); the pinning is via unit tests (rust oscore-fork lib.rs:3561, C oscore test_c8 :730). Fix: either add an interop vector or correct the sentence. Also related hygiene: legacy quarantine comments are stale (lichen/tests/pubkey_to_iid/main.c:42-49 claims literals encode the rejected SHA-512 profile while they hold upstream AddrForKey values; python test_vectors.py:2413-2422 docstring stale; test/vectors/legacy/yggdrasil-derivation.json ygg_addr fields were regenerated to upstream values).
